newsitem.title: USA: USA Waste to buy United Waste for $1.7 billion.
newsitem.headline: USA Waste to buy United Waste for $1.7 billion.

text.p: USA Waste Services Inc., the third-largest solid waste company in North America, has agreed to buy United Waste Systems Inc. in a stock swap valued at $1.7 billion, the companies said Monday.
Under the definitive agreement, USA Waste will offer 1.075 shares of its common stock for each United Waste share in a tax-free pooling of interests, they said.
United Waste's stock fell $5.25 on Nasdaq in late morning trading. USA Waste slid $3.25 to $32 on the New York Stock Exchange.

After the merger, USA Waste will have annual revenues of about $2.1 billion and assets of more than $4.5 billion, they said. The combined company will operate 155 landfills, 270 collection companies and 153 transfer stations serving over three million customers in 42 states, Washington, D.C., Canada, Mexico and Puerto Rico.

"We anticipate significant synergies and enhanced growth opportunities to result from this merger, which we expect will be accretive to our earnings," said John Drury, chairman and chief executive of USA Waste.

"United Waste's secondary market focus complements our predominantly urban market strategy. We are particularly enthusiastic about the $500 million in acquisition opportunities United Waste has identified in and around its existing service areas."
The deal is expected to close during the third quarter, subject to approval by the stockholders of the companies and regulators.
United Waste, the sixth-largest solid waste company in North America, will designate two persons to the board of USA Waste.
United Waste's senior management team will assist the merged company with transition matters and future acquisitions, the companies said.
USA Waste, based in Houston, serves over two million municipal, commercial, industrial and residential customers in 36 states with 119 landfills, 203 collection companies and 80 transfer stations.
United Waste, based in Greenwich, Conn., owns or operates 36 landfills, 67 collection companies and 73 transfer stations, serving more than 850,000 customers in 21 states.
Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp. acted as USA Waste's financial adviser. Goldman, Sachs & Co. acted as financial adviser to United Waste.
